title: Certificates of Deposit: The Credit Owed for a Penalty Charged in Grace
content:
This page fixes, for Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit, the size of the credit owed when a penalty was charged on money the owner took out during a grace period, and the cases in which no credit is written.

## Size of the credit

The credit is the full sum booked on the penalty entry, to the cent, with no further rounding and no recalculation. Part of such a penalty is never credited back on its own.

## When it is written

A credit is written only if every one of these holds for the penalty examined:

- its withdrawal was made during the grace period;
- that withdrawal was the owner's own;
- no reversal entry already points to the penalty;
- the booked penalty is above zero.

A withdrawal made outside the grace window yields no credit under these rules, and neither does a penalty failing any other condition above.

## Truth table (hypothetical penalty of USD 64.18)

| Made in grace | Owner's own | Already reversed | Credit written |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | No | USD 64.18 |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | nothing |
| Yes | No | No | nothing; a disputed transaction |
| No | Yes | No | nothing under these rules |
